question: does the raw source (WritingPrompts Arctic-Shift archive already on disk) supply created_utc + within-thread comment rank for the 7,008-row cw_community evaluation-valid population (methods/taste_decomposition/closure/cw_community/cw_honest_population.csv, matching cw_community_layer1.json's honest-population extension, pop_ext_manifest.json)?
answer: YES -- no new external fetching needed
data_source: datasets/creative-writing/writingprompts_comments.jsonl.gz (Arctic Shift API mirror of r/WritingPrompts, downloaded by datasets/creative-writing/download_writingprompts_v2.py; NOT the live Reddit API; already on disk on sk3, 994,546 top-level substantive comments). Exact-text join on sha1(story) against sha1(body) recovers created_utc/link_id/score verbatim (build_writingprompts_dataset.py concatenates 'PROMPT: '+title+'\n\nSTORY: '+body with NO further transformation, so story text is byte-identical to the raw comment body).
unmatched_bias_check: unmatched rows judgement rate .487 vs matched .502 -- no material selection bias
caveat_thread_pool: thread_rank/thread_size are computed within the POOL of substantive top-level comments the original download kept (>=200 chars, non-bot, non-deleted, top-level only) -- NOT the full raw Reddit thread (short/removed/bot replies are absent from the pool entirely, so thread_size understates true reply count). This is the same population definition the label itself (score>=10 among qualifying stories) is implicitly conditioned on, so it is the relevant reference class, not an approximation error.
protocol: GroupKFold(5) grouped by prompt_id (our content-hash prompt id; 5,067 distinct groups in the matched subset; 19/5067 prompt_ids map to >1 raw link_id and 3/5079 link_ids map to >1 prompt_id -- both <0.4%, not corrected for), pooled-OOF ROC-AUC, StandardScaler+LogisticRegression(class_weight='balanced'), all features standardized.
